note: Source of truth for the Roles page and the application form. The Core and Content Lead is appointed by the Network Custodian and is deliberately not listed. pdf paths assume the files in assets/roles/ are copied to public/roles/.

nature.title: Unpaid
nature.text: Every role is voluntary. There is no salary, allowance, stipend or payment of any kind, now or later.

nature.title: Not full-time
nature.text: You serve alongside your studies, work and family life. This is not a job, and a place on the team is not employment.

nature.title: Training is provided
nature.text: We train every volunteer in their role. Roles marked "Training provided" are open to people with no experience in the work, as long as you are willing to learn and to deliver. Roles marked "Experience required" need someone who has done the work before; you still receive onboarding.

nature.title: Project-based
nature.text: Outside Sunday there are no fixed hours. Work is organised by project on our internal tool, and you deliver what you agree to deliver.

nature.title: Sunday
nature.text: Sunday is the one firm commitment. After Holy Mass, core team members keep the day for the network.

nature.title: Online
nature.text: You can serve from anywhere in the world. We meet in person once a year, at the gathering on the last Saturday of October.

nature.title: Rooted in prayer
nature.text: You pray the Rosary daily and the Strangers' Prayer after it, and you may be invited to pray an extra Rosary for a stranger whose intention would otherwise go unprayed.

roles.title: Devotional Content Editor
roles.teamDescription: Core and Content keeps the Catholic core of the network untouched. It writes and approves everything strangers pray and read, keeps every word faithful to the Catechism of the Catholic Church, guards the intentions, and leads on safeguarding. Its head serves as the network's chaplain.
roles.summary: Builds and edits the daily prayer content members use in Youkaris.
roles.purpose: You build the prayer life of the network. You prepare the Rosary guides, novenas, litanies and Marian devotions strangers use in Youkaris, follow the liturgical calendar so each day has the right feasts and seasons, and make prayer simple enough for a beginner and rich enough for someone who has prayed for decades.
responsibilities: Prepare and maintain the Rosary guides for every set of mysteries, including short meditations for each decade.
Build the library of novenas, litanies and Marian devotions in Youkaris.
Keep the liturgical calendar in Youkaris accurate, including feasts, solemnities and Marian days.
Plan seasonal prayer for Advent, Lent, May and October.
Work with the Technology team so prayer content is structured, translatable and easy to update.
Lead the prayer and worship at the annual gathering with the Core and Content Lead.
requirements: A practising Catholic who prays the Rosary daily.
Good knowledge of traditional Catholic prayers, devotions and the liturgical year.
Careful, accurate work: one wrong word in a prayer is repeated by every stranger who prays it.
Clear writing in English.

questions.text: Why are you ideal for this role?
Tell us about a time you made something complicated simple for someone else to follow. What did you do?
Tell us about a time you had to get many small details exactly right. How did you make sure nothing slipped?

roles.title: Content Writer and Editor
roles.teamDescription: Core and Content keeps the Catholic core of the network untouched. It writes and approves everything strangers pray and read, keeps every word faithful to the Catechism of the Catholic Church, guards the intentions, and leads on safeguarding. Its head serves as the network's chaplain.
roles.summary: Writes and edits the daily words strangers read, faithful and alive.
roles.purpose: You write and edit what strangers read: daily reflections, teaching pieces, the words inside Youkaris and the copy that explains the network to the world. You work with priests who write reflections, edit them for clarity and length, and make sure every word sounds like Strangers for Mary: warm, direct, faithful and never preachy.
responsibilities: Write and edit daily reflections and short teaching pieces for Youkaris.
Edit reflections typed by invited priests for clarity, length and tone, without changing their teaching.
Write and maintain the words inside Youkaris: onboarding, reminders, messages and help text.
Keep a house style guide so every writer on the network sounds like one voice.
Work with Outreach on the website and campaign copy so it stays faithful.
Prepare content so it can be translated, starting with French.
requirements: A practising Catholic with good knowledge of the faith.
Excellent written English and a portfolio of published writing.
Strong editing skills: you make other people's writing clearer without losing their voice.
The discipline to deliver on time, every week.

questions.text: Why are you ideal for this role?
Tell us about a time you had to deliver writing to a tight deadline, week after week. How did you keep the quality up?
Tell us about a time someone disagreed with your edits. How did you handle it?

application.linkLabel: Links to three pieces of your writing

roles.title: Content Moderator
roles.teamDescription: Core and Content keeps the Catholic core of the network untouched. It writes and approves everything strangers pray and read, keeps every word faithful to the Catechism of the Catholic Church, guards the intentions, and leads on safeguarding. Its head serves as the network's chaplain.
roles.summary: Reviews the intentions members submit each week, by member ID only.
roles.purpose: You guard the intentions. Each Sunday, strangers submit one intention for the week. You review them by member ID only, never by name, against our intention guidelines: no full names, no identifying details, no long histories. You keep the exchange clean and safe, and you make sure anything that needs care reaches the right person quickly.
responsibilities: Review the week's intentions by member ID each Sunday, before the exchange begins.
Hold back or return intentions that break the guidelines, and help the stranger rewrite them.
Escalate anything that suggests someone may be at risk to the Safeguarding and Training Officer at once.
Use the admin portal to audit the exchange and flag outliers, such as repeated pairings.
Work with the Member Retention Coordinator so every intention is prayed for.
Keep and improve the intention guidelines with the Core and Content Lead.
requirements: A practising Catholic who prays daily.
Complete discretion and integrity: you will read what strangers have told no one else.
Calm judgement under time pressure on Sunday evenings.
Comfort working in a web-based admin tool.

questions.text: Why are you ideal for this role?
Tell us about a time you were trusted with sensitive information. How did you protect it?
Tell us about a time you had to make a judgement call quickly with incomplete information. What did you decide and why?

roles.title: Safeguarding and Training Officer
roles.teamDescription: Core and Content keeps the Catholic core of the network untouched. It writes and approves everything strangers pray and read, keeps every word faithful to the Catechism of the Catholic Church, guards the intentions, and leads on safeguarding. Its head serves as the network's chaplain.
roles.summary: Keeps members safe, and trains the team and the network.
roles.purpose: You keep the network safe and help it grow in faith. You write and run our safeguarding policy, handle concerns and disclosures properly, and make sure the core team and every partner understands their duties. You also lead formation: the teaching that helps strangers understand what they pray and why, and the formation offered at the gathering.
responsibilities: Write, maintain and train the core team on the safeguarding policy.
Receive and handle safeguarding concerns and disclosures, and keep secure records.
Advise on safety for the annual gathering and any in-person event.
Review how Youkaris handles messages, reports and blocking with the Technology team.
Plan formation for strangers: short teaching series on the faith, chastity and Catholic life.
Prepare formation sessions for the gathering with the Core and Content Lead.
requirements: A practising Catholic of mature judgement.
Willingness to complete recognised safeguarding training before starting, if you have not already.
Confidence teaching or presenting to groups.
Firmness when something is wrong, and gentleness with the person affected.
roles.reportsTo: Core and Content Lead, with a direct line to the Network Custodian for safeguarding concerns

questions.text: Why are you ideal for this role?
Tell us about a time you had to raise a difficult concern with someone. What happened?
Tell us about a time you taught or trained a group. How did you know it worked?

roles.title: Technology Lead
roles.teamDescription: Technology builds and runs Youkaris, the admin portal and the website: the systems that let a prayer typed in one country land safely in another. We build with a lot of AI assistance, so we look for engineers who can design systems, judge what AI produces and own what ships.
roles.summary: Owns the architecture of Youkaris, the admin portal and the website.
roles.purpose: You lead Technology and own the architecture of everything we build: Youkaris, the admin portal and the website. You make the big technical decisions, including when we build native and when we build hybrid, set the standards the team works to, and make sure what we ship is secure, private, affordable to run and ready to grow from hundreds of strangers to many thousands.
responsibilities: Own the system architecture across Youkaris, the admin portal and the website, on our Firebase backend.
Decide between native and hybrid approaches for mobile, and document why.
Set engineering standards: code review, testing, releases, security and privacy by design.
Lead the four other members of Technology: plan the work, review it and help them grow.
Set how the team uses AI tools safely and well, and review AI-generated code that touches core systems.
Keep running costs low: small media, sensible storage and archiving.
Protect stranger data: member IDs, no full names, and strict access by role.
Report progress to the leadership team in plain language.
requirements: Mid-level or senior engineer with real production experience and a strong grasp of system design.
Experience with Firebase or similar backends (Firestore, Cloud Functions, Auth), and with React.
Experience shipping mobile apps, native (Swift or Kotlin) or hybrid (React Native, Flutter or a PWA).
Daily, critical use of AI-assisted development tools.
The ability to lead and mentor other developers.

questions.text: Why are you the right person to lead our technology?
Tell us about a technical decision you made that turned out to be wrong. How did you find out, and what did you do?
Tell us about a time you helped a less experienced developer grow.

roles.title: Backend Engineer
roles.teamDescription: Technology builds and runs Youkaris, the admin portal and the website: the systems that let a prayer typed in one country land safely in another. We build with a lot of AI assistance, so we look for engineers who can design systems, judge what AI produces and own what ships.
roles.summary: Builds the intention exchange and the systems underneath Youkaris.
roles.purpose: You build the heart of Youkaris: the intention exchange. Each stranger submits one intention a week; each day from Monday to Saturday it is prayed for by a different stranger, and nobody ever receives their own. You build that engine and everything around it: member IDs, the reserve, the separate pool for strangers who have fallen away, reminders, archiving and the audit tools the admin team relies on.
responsibilities: Design and build the intention exchange so it is fair, random, auditable and never pairs a stranger with their own intention.
Build member IDs and role-based access so names are never attached to intentions.
Build the reserve and the separate pool so every intention is prayed for even when strangers miss days.
Build the reminders, three a day, and the missed-day flags.
Build archiving and deletion: intentions archived after their week and deleted after each gathering.
Write Cloud Functions, security rules and data models on Firebase, with tests.
Monitor performance, cost and errors in production.
requirements: Mid-level experience: you have shipped and maintained production software, not only tutorials or side projects.
Solid system design: you can reason about data models, APIs, queues, caching, security, cost and scale, and explain your trade-offs.
Fluent with AI-assisted development (for example Claude Code or Cursor): you know how to direct it, review what it produces and catch what it gets wrong.
Strong backend experience, ideally with Firebase (Firestore, Cloud Functions, security rules) or a similar platform.
Experience designing data models and scheduled or event-driven jobs.
Careful about privacy and security.

questions.text: Why are you ideal for this role?
Tell us about a production problem you diagnosed and fixed. What was the cause, and how did you find it?
Tell us about a time AI-generated code got something wrong. How did you catch it?

application.linkLabel: GitHub or links to your work

roles.teamDescription: Technology builds and runs Youkaris, the admin portal and the website: the systems that let a prayer typed in one country land safely in another. We build with a lot of AI assistance, so we look for engineers who can design systems, judge what AI produces and own what ships.
roles.summary: Builds Youkaris for the phones strangers carry every day.
roles.purpose: You build Youkaris for the phones strangers actually use, from the newest iPhone to a modest Android phone on a slow connection. We may move between native and hybrid as the network grows, so you are comfortable with both, and you care about speed, battery, offline use and reminders that arrive on time.
responsibilities: Build and maintain the Youkaris mobile experience for Android and iOS.
Implement prayer flows, intention submission, reminders and the liturgical calendar on mobile.
Make Youkaris work well on low-end Android phones and weak connections, including offline prayer.
Handle push notifications reliably across both platforms.
Manage releases to the Google Play Store and the Apple App Store.
Work with the Product Designer to make every screen simple and accessible.
requirements: Mid-level experience: you have shipped and maintained production software, not only tutorials or side projects.
Solid system design: you can reason about data models, APIs, queues, caching, security, cost and scale, and explain your trade-offs.
Fluent with AI-assisted development (for example Claude Code or Cursor): you know how to direct it, review what it produces and catch what it gets wrong.
Experience building and shipping native mobile apps for Android (Kotlin) and or iOS (Swift).
Experience with a hybrid approach too: React Native, Flutter, Capacitor or a progressive web app.
Experience with push notifications and store releases.

questions.text: Why are you ideal for this role?
Tell us about a time you had to choose between native and hybrid. What did you choose, and what happened?
Tell us about a release that went wrong. What did you do and what did you change afterwards?

application.linkLabel: App Store, Play Store or GitHub links

Build the admin portal: content management, intention review by ID, audits, volunteers and tasks.
Build the web version of Youkaris as a progressive web app.
Implement role-based access so each team sees only what it needs.
Keep the web fast, accessible and easy to translate.
Work with the Product Designer and the Brand and Graphic Designer on every page.

Strong React experience, with Next.js and TypeScript.
Experience building dashboards or admin tools with authentication and roles.
Good HTML and CSS, with a feel for design and accessibility.

Tell us about a time you disagreed with a designer or product owner. How did you resolve it?

roles.title: Product Designer (UX and UI)
roles.teamDescription: Technology builds and runs Youkaris, the admin portal and the website: the systems that let a prayer typed in one country land safely in another. We build with a lot of AI assistance, so we look for engineers who can design systems, judge what AI produces and own what ships.
roles.summary: Designs how Youkaris works and feels, screen by screen.
roles.purpose: You design how Youkaris works and feels. A stranger should be able to open the app half asleep at 6am and know exactly what to pray and for whom. You turn the network's way of life into flows and screens, test them with real strangers, and keep the app consistent with the Strangers for Mary brand.
responsibilities: Design the flows and screens of Youkaris and the admin portal.
Run simple user research and usability tests with real strangers.
Keep a design system in step with the brand, working with the Brand and Graphic Designer.
Design for accessibility, low-end phones and different languages.
Hand over clear, buildable designs to engineers and review what they build.
requirements: A portfolio of shipped product design for mobile and web apps.
Strong interaction design, information architecture and visual skills.
Fluency in Figma or a similar tool, and comfort working with AI design tools.
Understanding of how designs are built in React and on native platforms.

questions.text: Why are you ideal for this role?

Tell us about a time you had to defend a design decision. How did you make your case?

roles.title: Customer Experience Lead
roles.teamDescription: Stranger Relations is our customer experience team. It looks after every member from the day they join: onboarding, support, retention and events. It answers questions quickly, notices when someone misses a day and reaches out with care, so that nobody who joins is ever left alone.
roles.summary: Leads the team that onboards, supports and keeps every member.
roles.purpose: You lead Stranger Relations, our customer experience team. You own the full member journey: how people sign up, how they are onboarded, how quickly their questions are answered, how we keep them when they start to drift, and how the annual gathering runs. You set the standards, measure them and improve them. You sit on the leadership team with the other three team leads and report to the Network Custodian.
responsibilities: Lead the four other members of the team: set clear goals, review their work and help them grow.
Own the member journey from sign-up to first prayer to first gathering, and remove friction at every step.
Set service standards, such as response times and resolution rates, and report on them each month.
Own member retention: track who is active, who is drifting and who has left, and act on it.
Plan the annual gathering with the Events Coordinator and the Logistics Officer.
Bring member feedback to the leadership team and to Technology so the product keeps improving.
requirements: Experience leading a customer service, customer success, community or operations team.
Comfort with metrics and simple dashboards, and the habit of acting on them.
Calm, warm communication, including with people who are upset.
Strong organisation and follow-through.

questions.text: Why are you the right person to lead customer experience?
Tell us about a time you improved a customer or member metric. What did you change and what moved?
Tell us about a time you had to manage a team member who was not delivering.

roles.title: Onboarding Officer
roles.teamDescription: Stranger Relations is our customer experience team. It looks after every member from the day they join: onboarding, support, retention and events. It answers questions quickly, notices when someone misses a day and reaches out with care, so that nobody who joins is ever left alone.
roles.summary: Welcomes new members and gets them through their first weeks.
roles.purpose: You run onboarding. Most people who give up on a new habit do so in the first few weeks, so you make those weeks count: a clear welcome, a first Rosary that feels possible, a first intention written well and a check-in at the right moment. You track how many new members are still active after one, four and twelve weeks, and you keep improving the journey. You also help induct new volunteers.
responsibilities: Run the welcome journey for new members: messages, guides and first-week check-ins.
Help new members set up Youkaris, submit their first intention and pray their first Rosary.
Track early retention and report on it each month.
Improve onboarding with the Product Designer and the Content Writer.
Help induct new core team volunteers.
requirements: Warm, clear written and spoken communication.
Reliability: new members must hear from you on time.
Comfort with digital tools and spreadsheets.
Willingness to learn. Training is provided.

questions.text: Why are you ideal for this role?
Tell us about a time you helped someone new settle in, at work, school or in your community. What did you do?
Tell us about a time you had to follow up with many people on time. How did you stay on top of it?

roles.title: Customer Support Officer
roles.teamDescription: Stranger Relations is our customer experience team. It looks after every member from the day they join: onboarding, support, retention and events. It answers questions quickly, notices when someone misses a day and reaches out with care, so that nobody who joins is ever left alone.
roles.summary: Answers member questions and solves their problems, fast and with care.
roles.purpose: You run member support. When something goes wrong, such as an app that will not open, a reminder that did not arrive or an intention someone wants to change, you are who they reach. You answer quickly and kindly, solve what you can, escalate what you cannot with a clear report, and turn repeat problems into fixes and help articles.
responsibilities: Answer member questions by message, email and in Youkaris, within our response time targets.
Log issues and escalate technical problems to Technology with clear steps to reproduce.
Write and update help articles and answers to common questions.
Spot patterns in support requests and recommend improvements.
Cover the Sunday peak, when intentions close.
requirements: Patience, kindness and clear writing.
Basic technical confidence: you can follow steps, test and describe a problem.
Discretion with personal information.
Willingness to learn. Training is provided.

questions.text: Why are you ideal for this role?
Tell us about a time you dealt with someone who was frustrated or angry. What did you do, and how did it end?
Tell us about a problem you solved for someone that nobody else had been able to fix.

roles.title: Member Retention Coordinator
roles.teamDescription: Stranger Relations is our customer experience team. It looks after every member from the day they join: onboarding, support, retention and events. It answers questions quickly, notices when someone misses a day and reaches out with care, so that nobody who joins is ever left alone.
roles.summary: Keeps members active, and makes sure every intention is covered.
roles.purpose: You own retention and coverage. When members miss days, Youkaris flags it; you make sure they get support rather than blame, and that their assigned intentions are covered the same day by reserve members. You coordinate the reserve, which starts with the core team and grows by invitation, look after members who have fallen away, and report every week on coverage and re-engagement.
responsibilities: Monitor missed-day flags and make sure each member at risk is contacted with care.
Coordinate the reserve so every uncovered intention is prayed for the same day.
Invite consistent members to join the reserve, with the Customer Experience Lead.
Run re-engagement for members who have fallen away.
Work with the Backend Engineer on how missed days and the reserve work in Youkaris.
Report weekly on coverage and re-engagement.
requirements: Strong organisation and follow-through on short deadlines.
Gentle, encouraging communication.
Comfort with dashboards and simple data.
Willingness to pray an extra Rosary at short notice when needed.

questions.text: Why are you ideal for this role?
Tell us about a time you had to coordinate several people against a deadline. What did you do when someone dropped out?
Tell us about a time you encouraged someone to keep going when they wanted to give up.

roles.title: Events Coordinator

It answers questions quickly, notices when someone misses a day and reaches out with care, so that nobody who joins is ever left alone.
roles.summary: Plans and runs the annual gathering and the member experience on the day.
roles.purpose: You plan and run the annual gathering on the last Saturday of October: the programme, the schedule, the volunteers and the experience of every member on the day. Holy Mass is at the centre of every gathering, and gatherings are never ticketed. You work with the Logistics Officer on venue, transport and supplies, with Core and Content on worship and formation, and with the Finance Officer on the budget. You also keep the roll of members who have died, so the network keeps praying for them.
responsibilities: Plan the gathering programme, schedule and run of show.
Recruit, brief and lead event-day volunteers.
Work with the Logistics Officer on venue, transport, food and supplies.
Work with the Finance Officer on the event budget, paid for by the network's own work, never by tickets.
Collect feedback after each gathering and report what to improve.
Keep the roll of members gone before us and organise prayer for them.
requirements: Strong organisation and attention to detail.
Calm under pressure on the day.
Clear communication with volunteers and suppliers.
Willingness to learn. Training is provided.

questions.text: Why are you ideal for this role?
Tell us about an event or project you organised. What was your part and how did it go?
Tell us about a time a plan fell apart at the last minute. What did you do?

It builds the brand, tells our story on every channel, wins partners, runs campaigns for the causes we serve, moves people and goods where they need to be, and keeps the network's money clean and accountable. A strong, marketable brand is what funds our charity and outreach.
roles.summary: Leads marketing, partnerships, campaigns and the network's revenue.
roles.purpose: You lead Outreach, our marketing, sales and partnerships team. You own growth: the brand, the marketing plan, member acquisition, partnerships with companies, campaigns for our causes and the income-generating work that funds them. You set targets, lead the team to hit them and report the results. You sit on the leadership team with the other three team leads and report to the Network Custodian.
responsibilities: Lead the four other members of the team: set clear goals, review their work and help them grow.
Own the marketing plan and member acquisition targets, and report on them each month.
Find, pitch and manage partnerships with companies that help with brand visibility, marketing and product development.
Plan and run campaigns for our causes: orphaned children, the chastity and formation of young people, and justice and peace.
Lead merchandise and other sales with the Brand and Graphic Designer, the Logistics Officer and the Finance Officer.
Protect the brand and make sure the network's money is handled with no cash and full transparency.
requirements: Experience leading marketing, sales, partnerships or business development.
Strong judgement about brand and what makes it marketable.
Confidence pitching to and negotiating with company leaders.
Ability to lead creative people and set measurable targets.

questions.text: Why are you the right person to lead marketing and partnerships?
Tell us about a deal, partnership or sale you closed. How did you win it?

Write and keep the brand guidelines so anyone on the network can use the brand correctly.
Design social media graphics, campaigns, documents and presentations.
Design merchandise and the visual identity of the annual gathering.
Work with the Product Designer so Youkaris and the website feel like one brand.
Review everything that carries the brand before it goes out.
Direct photography and choose imagery that shows real young people living the faith.

A portfolio with at least two complete brand identities or brand systems you designed or led.
Expert typography, layout and colour skills.
Fluency in professional design tools (Figma, Adobe Illustrator and Photoshop or equivalents) and comfort with AI tools.

Consistency: you post on schedule and track results.

roles.title: Logistics Officer
roles.teamDescription: Outreach is our marketing, sales and partnerships team. roles.purpose: You run logistics for the network. When a campaign delivers help to a cause, when merchandise ships to members, or when the annual gathering needs a venue, transport, food and supplies, you plan it, source it, track it and make sure it arrives. You work with suppliers, keep stock and delivery records, and keep costs inside budget.

Source and manage suppliers, venues, transport and delivery partners.
Keep stock, orders and delivery records accurate and up to date.
Work with the Finance Officer so every purchase is approved and paid without cash.
Work with the Events Coordinator on everything the gathering needs on the day.
Report on delivery times, costs and problems, and fix what keeps going wrong.
requirements: Strong organisation, planning and attention to detail.
Clear communication with suppliers and partners.
Comfort with spreadsheets and simple tracking tools.
Willingness to learn. Training is provided.

roles.title: Finance Officer (Treasurer)
roles.teamDescription: Outreach is our marketing, sales and partnerships team. It builds the brand, tells our story on every channel, wins partners, runs campaigns for the causes we serve, moves people and goods where they need to be, and keeps the network's money clean and accountable. A strong, marketable brand is what funds our charity and outreach.
roles.summary: Keeps the books, controls the money and reports it openly.
roles.purpose: You run the network's finances. The network never takes cash and no member physically handles network money: everything passes through a merchant code or bank account with clear access rules. You set up and run those controls, keep the books, prepare budgets, track campaign and merchandise income, and publish clear reports so every member can trust how the money is used.
responsibilities: Set up and run the bank account and merchant code, with clear access and approval rules.
Make sure the network never takes cash and no member handles network money.
Keep accurate books and publish financial reports to the leadership team and the network.
Prepare budgets for technology, events, logistics and campaigns.
Track merchandise and campaign income with the Marketing and Partnerships Lead and the Logistics Officer.
requirements: Experience in accounting, finance or bookkeeping.
Complete honesty and attention to detail.
Confidence with spreadsheets and accounting tools.
Understanding of mobile money, merchant codes and online payments.
roles.reportsTo: Marketing and Partnerships Lead, and accountable to the Network Custodian for the network's finances

questions.text: Why are you ideal for this role?
